title: Features: CLI, server, MCP, web, editor and cloud
summary:
This part settles every user-visible feature of RichView's surfaces outside the report itself: the `richview` commands, the MCP server, publishing and RichView Cowork, the self-hosted server, the VS Code extension, the website (home, playground, flagship, docs, routes, headers and share images), agent knowledge, the generated npm packages and asset upload. One card per feature, grouped by surface; each says keep, change or drop and gives the rewrite's behaviour, and the last card names the checks that prove the new behaviour. Chart features (04a), report rendering (04b), branch-only features (04d), types (05), styles and motion (06) and budgets (07) are out of scope; cards point there.

Key decisions:

- **Commands and MCP** (FEA-SF-01, FEA-SF-09): ten commands with only the flags listed, `asset` among them now that uploads return (INT-31), plus `report` if FEA-SF-53 is accepted; seven MCP tools, each the twin of a CLI command.
- **Publishing without surprises** (FEA-SF-12, FEA-SF-13, FEA-SF-51, FEA-SF-52): no default server, no token in tool arguments, a distinct result for an unchanged or conflicting version, automatic first publication and protection against creating a second address by mistake, and links to report files that keep working once published.
- **What RichView Cowork's first cut offers** (FEA-SF-14 to FEA-SF-20, FEA-SF-53, FEA-SF-54): latest by SemVer with an owner pin, versions kept until the owner deletes them, a report list that shows each caller only what is shared with them (OPN-54), regenerate kept for the owner, the render API dropped, a report menu with share and protect, owner actions in the CLI, and the enterprise-grade roles and governance section that Cowork gets from the server core it shares with Publish (FEA-SF-19, Daniel's answer).
- **Previews keep the last good render** (FEA-SF-08, FEA-SF-23, FEA-SF-24, FEA-SF-27): `serve` and VS Code show diagnostics in a banner above the last good render, the Problems panel shows exactly what `richview validate` returns, and Export writes what `generate` writes.
- **An honest site** (FEA-SF-28, FEA-SF-30, FEA-SF-46, FEA-SF-55, FEA-SF-60, FEA-SF-61): three header links; ten home-page statements dropped or rewritten when the rewrite reaches `prod`, with no hotfix to the live page (FEA-SF-30, OPN-43); a closed route map; share images without findings, and a thumbnail for every story with an address (INT-07); a Content Security Policy on site pages; and a crawler policy in the repository.
- **Agent surfaces** (FEA-SF-47, FEA-SF-48, FEA-SF-61, FEA-SF-65): `learn`, the skill and `llms.txt` generated from or checked against the code so they cannot drift (INT-21, INT-66), a crawler policy that lets agents and models find the docs, and a measurement that scores fresh-agent runs on real tasks and tracks the scores over time, so RichView changes until agents understand it as easily as possible (INT-21).
- **Try paths** (FEA-SF-21, FEA-SF-33 to FEA-SF-35, FEA-SF-42, FEA-SF-43): the playground linked from the docs now and the header at launch, the extension on the VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX for macOS arm64 and Linux x64 (INT-71), a downloadable first report and a docs gallery with one focused page per chart type.

25 of the 65 cards offer options (FEA-SF-04, FEA-SF-09, FEA-SF-13, FEA-SF-15, FEA-SF-16, FEA-SF-17, FEA-SF-18, FEA-SF-19, FEA-SF-21, FEA-SF-28, FEA-SF-33, FEA-SF-35, FEA-SF-36, FEA-SF-37, FEA-SF-38, FEA-SF-45, FEA-SF-51, FEA-SF-52, FEA-SF-53, FEA-SF-55, FEA-SF-57, FEA-SF-58, FEA-SF-60, FEA-SF-61 and FEA-SF-65); the rest confirm one proposal. VS Code cards have no screenshots: the extension cannot run headless on the capture host. The `serve` preview, PDF output and published report pages were captured from the b4db233 release build. Where `main` and live richview.ai differ (the live site is built from unmerged PR #69), cards say which they describe.

Answers here interact with other parts; each card names the other side under conflicts:

- FEA-SF-01, FEA-SF-05, FEA-SF-08 and FEA-SF-23 follow FEA-RP-31 (no report card) and FEA-RP-33 (no `theme`), which TYP-71 and TYP-98 do not yet follow.
- FEA-SF-04 takes its widths from FEA-CH-64 and its browser pass from FEA-CH-59, against TYP-71's 720 px default.
- FEA-SF-06 and FEA-SF-27 keep the editor's export to HTML, against TYP-98's `output` and `page` parameters.
- FEA-SF-13 and FEA-SF-51 add codes and a `new` field that TYP-55, TYP-66 and TYP-69 lack.
- FEA-SF-14 and FEA-SF-54 follow TYP-64 and TYP-96 for retention and latest.
- FEA-SF-15 and FEA-SF-17 change which reads INT-36's earlier proposal left open; FEA-SF-18 needs no list token, because the menu uses the server's sign-in (OPN-54).
- FEA-SF-19, Daniel's answer, gives both servers enterprise-grade roles, so the share and protect actions he asked for on 2026-10-12 return with them.
- FEA-SF-24 depends on ARC-08 moving the editor's checks into core.
- FEA-SF-30 and FEA-SF-45 ship no legacy hotfix: the live page changes when the rewrite reaches `prod`, and the reel's render changes no deployed code (OPN-02, OPN-43).
- FEA-SF-36 keeps the reading position but not chart state across styles.
- FEA-SF-39 removes the lightbox from ARC-41.
- FEA-SF-43 and FEA-SF-46 follow FEA-BR-22's per-type pages and FEA-BR-12's famous-charts page when those are accepted.
- FEA-SF-48 describes the generated files that return after OPN-31.
- FEA-SF-52 makes linked files public, against TYP-65 and TYP-70.
- FEA-SF-60 extends ARC-15's policy to the static site.

Some conflicts notes in other parts were written against an earlier draft of this part; where one disagrees with a card here, the card's current text is what an answer accepts.

How to answer: **accept** keeps the proposal as written (where options are listed, the proposal is the recommendation); **edit** replaces it with your text; **reject** drops the feature from the rewrite (add a note with what you want instead); **defer** leaves it open. Part 08's cross-part contradiction cards (OPN-50 to OPN-68) decide conflicts involving this part's cards and should be answered first.

items.title: `richview init`: start a report folder
items.question: Does `init` keep scaffolding a report folder, and what does the template contain?
items.why: The template is the first report a person sees and the model an agent copies. Today it hard-codes `styles: [sleek]` while the renderer defaults to brutalist, writes no `slug`, so a later title edit moves the published address (FEA-SF-13), and a second run fails with a misleading `report.root.shared` error and exit 2.
items.proposed: Keep `richview init [dir] [--name report]`: it creates the folder and writes the template without ever overwriting. The template is the build-embedded `examples/hello-world/` folder, also served as the MCP example resource (FEA-SF-11): frontmatter with `title`, `description`, `version: 0.0.1`, `slug` and `styles` naming the default style (D-DEFAULT-STYLE, part 06); one metric, one chart reading block-local `data/visits.csv`, which `init` writes beside it, and one callout. It renders and checks with no warning. An existing file stops with “<path> already exists; nothing was written” and exit 1. The success message names `richview serve` and `richview check`.

items.title: `richview validate`: structure without rendering
items.question: Does `validate` stay the fast structural check, with a mode that runs the publish rules?
items.why: Agents call `validate` after every edit because it is the cheapest check. It already parses, checks block schemas and confirms that referenced files exist. There is no way to run the publish rules locally except by publishing, although TYP-07 assumes a `validate --publish`.
items.proposed: Keep `richview validate <input>`: parse the source, check every block against its schema and confirm that each referenced file exists inside the report folder, without rendering charts. `--publish` adds the publish rules (TYP-07: `title`, `description`, `version` and a valid slug), so an agent can preflight without a server; the MCP tool takes the same flag. Output and exit codes follow TYP-68 and TYP-54. Chart geometry stays with `check`.

items.title: `richview check`: rendered chart geometry
items.question: Does `check` measure each chart at the widths it will occupy, by default?
items.why: `check` is how an agent learns that labels clip or collide before a human looks. Today it measures one chart width per run (default 720 px), a width no builtin figure occupies: FEA-CH-64 renders figures at the phone column (358 px) and the style's text measure (512–576 px in the builtins). Phone-width problems need a second run that neither the docs nor the learn bundle ask for. FEA-CH-59 adds a browser glyph pass to `check` at phone and desktop widths.
items.proposed: Keep `richview check <input> [--style …] [--chart-width …] [--format]`: render the report and return every render diagnostic plus per-chart geometry (clipping, collisions, dropped labels with provenance). By default each chart is checked at the widths it occupies for readers (STY-30, TYP-89): the phone column (358 px) and the style's text measure, plus the report width for a figure set full-width. Repeatable `--chart-width` replaces them (range: TYP-72). Each chart result names its width. Checks read the engine's geometry model, which the WebGL page and the PDF's vector output both draw (Daniel's INT-31 answer). If FEA-CH-59 keeps a browser glyph pass, which depends on FEA-CH-30's open text question, it runs at the same widths where a local browser exists, and its results say they were measured in a browser (ARC-08). `--style` checks the report in another style without editing it. Readability findings are results, not failures: the exit code is 1 only when an `error` exists (TYP-54).

options.detail: Fastest; measures a width no builtin figure has, and phone problems surface only when someone asks for them.

items.title: `richview generate`: write the self-contained report
items.question: Does `generate` write one self-contained HTML file into the report's `Rendered/` folder, from any working directory?
items.why: This file is what readers receive. Today a chart report fails with `report.output.runtime` (exit 2) unless the command runs where `./dist/web` holds a built site, `RICHVIEW_PUBLIC_DIR` points at one, or the site tree sits at `<binary dir>/../share/richview/web` or `<binary dir>/../public`; a binary copied on its own cannot export a chart report (reproduced at b4db233). Working from any directory is a change that ARC-07's embedded runtime makes possible.
items.proposed: Keep `richview generate <input>` (alias `g`): it writes `<report folder>/Rendered/<stem>.html`, self-contained as FEA-RP-38 defines, and copies the files that links point to beside it (FEA-RP-40). `-o` names another file inside `Rendered/`. Repeatable `--style` overrides the source's `styles` for this output only. It works from any working directory because the runtime is embedded (ARC-07). A report with block errors is still written so the author can see it, and the command exits 1 (TYP-54); PDF output refuses on errors instead (FEA-RP-44, FEA-SF-06). There is no `--report-card` (FEA-RP-31) and no `--theme` (FEA-RP-33).

items.title: Readable terminal output
items.question: Should the default (non-JSON) output show each diagnostic's line and code, once?
items.why: INT-21 promises that every error names the line and the fix. The default output prints `[error] chart.type: expected …` without the line or code that the JSON carries (`line: 362`); `check` prints every diagnostic twice; a report with nine charts repeats the same info line nine times; and `init` prints a serialized JSON array as its error.
items.proposed: The default output prints one line per diagnostic as `<file>:<line> <level> <code>: <message>`, with the block path when there is no line. Identical `info` diagnostics collapse into one line with a count. Diagnostics go to standard error; the result line (“Generated …”, “Valid, 22 rich blocks”) goes to standard output. A failure prints one sentence, never serialized JSON. `--format json` follows TYP-68.

items.title: `richview serve`: live preview in a browser
items.question: Does `serve` stay a preview of one report that survives broken edits?
items.why: `serve` is the preview for authors without VS Code and for watching an agent work. Today it refuses to start when the source cannot render; once running, a breaking edit replaces the page with raw JSON, and because that page has no poller the preview stays on the JSON after the source is fixed, until the author reloads by hand (reproduced). It also writes `tmp/richview-preview` into the current directory and serves the whole website and the unauthenticated render API.
items.proposed: Keep `richview serve <input> [-p 4711] [--bind 127.0.0.1] [--style …]`: it serves the rendered report and reloads it within a second of any change in the report folder (`Rendered/` ignored). Diagnostics appear in a banner above the report, outside the report's own HTML (FEA-RP-31). A hard error keeps the last good render under that banner and recovers on its own when the source is fixed; a broken source at startup shows the banner instead of refusing to start. It writes nothing outside `Rendered/` (ARC-10) and serves only the preview, its runtime, its revision poll and, at `/thumbnail`, the 1200×630 link-preview thumbnail of the story as it would be published, rendered on demand (ARC-69), on loopback unless `--bind` says otherwise (ARC-24). The page itself carries no `og:` tags (FEA-RP-51). `--bind` stays for checking on a phone over the local network. `--theme`, `--format`, `--public-dir` and `--allow-network` go (FEA-SF-01).

items.title: MCP tools
items.question: What can an agent do through RichView's MCP server (`richview mcp`): which tools does it get?
items.why: The tool list is an agent's whole vocabulary for RichView, what INT-69's fresh-agent test exercises and what FEA-SF-65 scores over time (INT-21). It grew from four (dec-56) to five (`learn`, PR #4) to seven (two asset tools, 2026-10-11), and FEA-RP-62 adds two more. TYP-69 fixes each tool's contract once this list is settled.
items.proposed:
| Tool | Does | CLI twin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `richview_learn` | Returns the knowledge bundle or one section | `learn` |
| `richview_validate` | Structure and file checks; optional publish rules | `validate` |
| `richview_check` | Render plus chart geometry | `check` |
| `richview_render` | Writes `Rendered/` HTML or PDF | `generate` |
| `richview_publish` | Publishes a version to a named server | `publish` |
| `richview_asset_put` | Uploads a data or media file and returns its pinned reference, with progress notifications | `asset put` |
| `richview_asset_verify` | Checks stored objects against pinned references | `asset verify` |
| `richview_image_search` | Searches Unsplash and returns candidate photos with their credit fields; registers no download (FEA-RP-62) | `image search` |
| `richview_image_use` | Registers the download once and returns paste-ready YAML for an image block or `title_image` (FEA-RP-62) | `image use` |

Nine tools: the five core tools, the two asset tools, which return with uploads (INT-31, ARC-34, FEA-SF-50), and the two image tools that Daniel accepted in FEA-RP-62. Store credentials come only from the MCP host's environment or the credentials file a store profile names, never from tool arguments (ARC-23). The Unsplash key comes only from `UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY` in the MCP host's environment, never from tool arguments (FEA-RP-62). No tool deletes, pins or regenerates stored versions (FEA-SF-53). Each tool runs the same operation as its CLI twin and returns the same JSON (ARC-08, TYP-69). Annotations use MCP's meanings. `readOnlyHint` marks a tool that changes no state: `learn`, `validate`, `check`, `asset_verify` and `image_search`. `openWorldHint` marks a tool that reaches beyond the machine: `publish`, both asset tools and both image tools. `image_use` is not read-only, because it registers a download with Unsplash. Tool descriptions are generated with the learn bundle (INT-66).

options.label: Nine tools, core, asset and image
options.detail: The five core tools plus upload and verify, which Daniel's INT-31 answer keeps, and the two image tools of FEA-RP-62; an agent can host large data and media and find a photo without leaving MCP.

items.recommendation: Nine tools, core, asset and image: every tool maps to a command the docs teach, and uploads and image search are part of the rewrite (INT-31, FEA-SF-50, FEA-RP-62).

items.title: Publishing from the CLI, MCP and VS Code
items.question: How do the three publish clients behave in the rewrite?
items.why: Publishing is RichView's one outward action. Today the CLI and VS Code default to `https://richview.uk`, a v2 page with no report API; the MCP tool accepts the token as an argument; republishing an existing version with changed content prints “Published <url>” although nothing was stored; and `--theme` is accepted and silently not sent. The rules below come from the cards named in the last column; this card applies them to the three clients.
items.proposed:
| Rule | CLI `richview publish` | MCP `richview_publish` | VS Code Publish | Decided in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Server | `--server` or `RICHVIEW_SERVER`, required | only a server configured in the MCP host's environment (`RICHVIEW_SERVER`); an optional `server` argument must name it, and any other server is refused | workspace setting, asked for once | TYP-67, OPN-04, INT-79 |
| Token | `RICHVIEW_TOKEN` or `--token`, sent only to the server it is configured for | the MCP host's environment only, sent only to the configured server | secret storage per server | ARC-23, INT-79 |
| Slug | `--slug`, frontmatter, then title | `slug`, frontmatter, then title | frontmatter, then title | TYP-61, FEA-SF-13 |
| Result | new version, unchanged republish or version conflict, with slug, version, `url` and `permalink` | the same JSON | the same, with Copy link and Open | TYP-63, TYP-68 |
| First address | automatic | automatic | automatic | FEA-SF-51 |
| Create another address for this file | `--new` | `new: true` | a confirmation dialog | FEA-SF-51 |

A token is bound to the server it was configured for and is never sent anywhere else: `RICHVIEW_TOKEN` goes only to `RICHVIEW_SERVER`, and publishing to another server with `--server` needs that server's own token. An agent cannot choose where a token goes, so text injected into a source file or a dataset cannot send it to a server of its choosing (INT-79). All three send the same request (ARC-20, TYP-66). No client accepts `--style` or `--theme`: the published look is what the source declares.

In VS Code, publishing is one click: a Publish button on an open `.rmd` and a right-click Publish command in the editor and the explorer, each sending this same request (FEA-SF-30).

items.question: Do the reader routes keep these URLs under the new rules for latest and retention?
items.why: These are the URLs people share. | Route | Serves | Cache |
| --- | --- | --- |

items.title: Confirmation before a new report address
items.question: When should creating a report address need confirmation?
items.why: Publishing should create the first report in one command. After that, a mistyped slug or a title change should not silently create another report.
items.proposed: The CLI, MCP and VS Code create a report on its first publish to a server. The result names its address and version. New reports use the server’s visibility default (private unless configured otherwise). The clients remember a successful publish by local source path and server. Later requests from the same file and computer expect an existing address. If the slug is unused, the server returns HTTP 409 and publish.new-slug and stores nothing. To deliberately create another address, use CLI --new, MCP new: true or the VS Code confirmation. For POST /api/reports, omitting new permits creation and new: false requires an existing report. items.why: On 2026-10-18 Daniel moved the chart gallery into the docs as “a browsable index of ALL actually supported chart types, each clickable into a focused chart example with relevant source/authoring guidance and functioning interactions”, adding “The gallery is not one long end-to-end report.” His review the same day required it to “visibly display real RichView-rendered charts with matching source and functioning relevant interactions for every supported type”. The live gallery (unmerged PR #69) is one page: on 2026-10-22 all nine figures offered Table, Download SVG, Download CSV and Expand, Expand worked on nine of nine, and the page logged no errors (headless probe). It links three routes that return 404. The last harness run's “0 of 36” for the modal and SVG export meant it found no such controls to drive, which contradicts the run before it (Expand present 36 of 36).
items.proposed: `/docs/charts` is an index of every supported chart type (nine today; Daniel's FEA-CH-01 answer extends them to every type of ggplot2, Plotly, ECharts, Highcharts and Power BI, likely around 30, compiled under TYP-14's open item) and of the map and flow elements, each entry with a small live chart and one sentence on when to use it, opening `/docs/charts/<type>`. A type page shows the live chart rendered by the report runtime, its complete `.rmd` source with Copy and “Open in playground” (FEA-SF-34), the fields that matter for that type and every interaction the type supports. FEA-BR-22 owns this index-plus-pages shape; this card fixes the content and its checks: the release run exercises every type page's interactions at phone and desktop widths (DEL-59, DEL-81), a supported type without a page fails the build (FEA-BR-22), and no page links a route that does not exist (OPN-19).

items.title: Share images and link previews
items.question: Which pages carry a share image, and what may it show?
items.why: Link previews are often the first thing people see of RichView. Today the home page declares `/landing/og.png`, which shows the retired tagline and “BETA · richview.ai” (OPN-20 replaces both in the rewrite). The flagship declares its own `og.png`: a three-style collage of the report's title and verdict, which INT-45 rules out for share images. Docs, gallery, playground and legal pages declare no preview metadata. Published reports carry no `og:` metadata today; FEA-RP-51 gives them `og:title` and `og:description`, and with this card's thumbnail `og:image`. Daniel's INT-07 answer gives every story with an address a rich link preview wherever its link is shared, and no other card decides what the image shows or how it is produced.

Signed-in readers with access see the title and thumbnail. The card is the same for a story that is private, missing or deleted, in status, headers and bytes, so an anonymous request cannot tell them apart | The same rule for the tags (FEA-RP-51) |

The server renders a story's thumbnail once per version, stores it beside the version and serves it from the same access check as the story, so no preview request renders anything. items.title: Security headers on richview.ai
items.question: Do richview.ai's pages send a Content Security Policy, and which responses allow cross-origin reads?
items.why: `assets/_headers` sends `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` on every response and `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on `/richview_web.js`, `/richview_web_bg.wasm` and `/bootstrap.js`; no response carries a Content Security Policy or `frame-ancestors` (checked live). ARC-15's policy covers report hosts and exported reports, not the site, which renders visitor-edited source in the playground and the home demo. Those previews run in opaque-origin sandboxed frames (ARC-14) and load the runtime from the site, which is what the CORS header is for.
items.proposed: Every response keeps `nosniff` and the referrer policy. Reports the site serves, such as the flagship's renders, carry ARC-15's policy like any report. Site pages send a policy that loads scripts, styles, fonts, images and connections from richview.ai only, allows the renderer's inline styles and `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, frames only richview.ai pages and the previews the page renders, and sets `base-uri 'none'` and `frame-ancestors 'self'`. The runtime files the sandboxed previews load keep `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`; no other response allows cross-origin reads. The site suites run with these headers and fail on any policy violation (DEL-59).

options.label: Policy on site pages
options.detail: An injection into a page or a preview can run only richview.ai's own code; every page and preview must be tested under the policy, or pages break.

options.label: Headers as today
options.detail: Nothing to maintain; an injection in visitor-edited previews or a page runs with no policy behind it.

items.recommendation: Policy on site pages.

items.title: Crawler and AI-use policy
items.question: What does richview.ai tell search engines and AI crawlers?
items.why: RichView is built for agents: the site serves `llms.txt` and the skill to them (FEA-SF-48), and Daniel's INT-21 answer makes agents that learn, write, check and publish RichView on their own a headline bet, so how agents and the models behind them find and read the docs matters. Today `/robots.txt` is a file Cloudflare manages, absent from the repository: 24 lines of content-signal definitions with no `User-agent` or `Content-Signal` line, so by its own terms it neither grants nor restricts any use.
items.proposed: The site ships its own `/robots.txt`: every crawler may fetch every page of the route map (FEA-SF-46), with `Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=yes`. The deploy that ships it checks that `/robots.txt` serves these lines (DEL-40).

items.question: Do the skill and `llms.txt` stay, checked against the code and served on the site?

Their seven MCP tools are right today; FEA-SF-09 grows the list to nine with the two image tools (FEA-RP-62). `skill/reference/anti-slop.md` is one of four copies of the design rules (OPN-32), and `docs/AGENT-QUICKSTART.md` repeats the six chart types. The skill is neither served nor packaged, and `llms.txt` is not served: `richview.ai/llms.txt` returns 404.
items.proposed: Keep both, generated from or checked against the code (INT-21, INT-66), so the drift Daniel's INT-21 answer names cannot return. `skill/SKILL.md` stays a short guide to judgement and workflow (assertion titles, sourced claims, check before sharing, publish only when asked; guidance for agents, not a judgment of a story by RichView, INT-77) that sends the agent to `richview learn` for every fact (ARC-52); its design principles come from part 06's single design-rule source instead of `skill/reference/anti-slop.md` (OPN-32). items.title: Roles, approvals and tenant isolation are tested on every route
items.question: How is it proven that Cowork's and Publish's roles and approvals hold, and that hosted Cowork keeps accounts apart?
items.why: A leaked private report is invisible in a screenshot review and breaks the safety floor (INT-79). Roles are now part of RichView (INT-06), and hosted Cowork serves many accounts (INT-36).
items.proposed:
A role, route and action matrix generated from the server's route table (TYP-70) runs against the server core on loopback, in the release run for any batch that touches the server core or its routes (DEL-81). For every route, assets, downloads, previews, link-preview tags and thumbnails, search, feeds and old releases included, each role (anonymous, reader, author, owner and admin; Publish's editor, super editor and publishing service; the final set follows FEA-SF-19's enterprise-grade roles), the governance section's routes included, gets the expected allow or deny, and a denial reveals nothing, with the same answer for missing and forbidden. A story shared only with signed-in readers gives an anonymous request, a link-preview crawler included, no title, description or image of the story (INT-07, FEA-SF-55); every response for such a story carries `private, no-store`, and the matrix checks that a story unshared after a read is refused on the next request through the same cache. A route with no row fails the gate.

Approvals bind the exact head; a changed head voids them; nobody approves their own change; a role change voids outstanding approvals (FEA-BR-26). The browser source edit refuses a report that fails to validate or render, saves nothing and shows the diagnostics (INT-26). On hosted Cowork, two accounts are refused each other's reports on every route, and limits on report count and size are enforced with a clear error (INT-36). Server cases join the hostile-input corpus (DEL-56): path traversal in slugs, tokens in URLs, cross-site requests on state-changing routes.

items.title: The reader's bar above a hosted report
items.question: Does the report host put anything of its own around a report, and what may it say?
items.why: A reader who opens a shared report cannot tell whose it is, who else can open it or where to find it again, and its author has no way from the report back to its page. Reports are served as stored (FEA-SF-14, ARC-21), so anything the host adds is new scope. A public report's response is cached for everyone (FEA-SF-14), so whatever the host adds to it is the same for every reader, and who may see which report follows FEA-SF-19 and OPN-54.
items.proposed: *The report host shows one slim bar above a report and nothing else around it.* It is 44px tall, static at the top (it scrolls away and never covers or overlays the report), in the site's paper and ink, and has four states: the author's own report (its badge, "Shared with N people", a Share button back to its page); a report shared with the reader by name ("Shared with you · by {owner} · {organization}", "Find it again under Shared with me"); a report the reader's organization can open ("From {organization} · every member can open it", "All reports"); and a public report ("anyone with the link can open it", "Sign in"). Every reader of a public version sees the same bar, including its author. When a new version's published style declares company.name, put that name and its optional validated company.logo before the access message. The mark fills the bar's height (24px, 20px under 640px) and its width follows its shape, up to 180px (120px under 640px). A mark wider than 2.5 times its height is a lockup that carries the name: show it alone, with the name as its alt text. A squarer mark keeps the mark and the name side by side; on a phone the name stays on one line in the bar's own text size and ends in an ellipsis when it does not fit, and never pushes the primary action out. The class is decided when the version is published, from the stored image's dimensions; the browser measures nothing. Use company.logo-dark on dark reports when available, otherwise give the standard mark a light backing. Keep the name and primary action readable on phones. The hosted screen shows the mark once. Print and standalone exports retain the report's title treatment. Store the credit with that version. Existing versions and versions without a name keep the previous bar, including "Published with RichView" on public links. Only the published style supplies public attribution. Personal accounts and sharing records supply no credit. The host owns the HTML and CSS, escapes the name and accepts only still PNG, JPEG or WebP marks within STY-72's validated size limits. Access rules, controls and caching follow FEA-SF-19, OPN-54 and FEA-SF-14. The server inserts it at serve time like the preview tags, with every value escaped; the report's own HTML and its CSP stay as they are (its policy already allows inline styles). Mock-ups: `mockups/host-*.html`.

items.title: Measuring how well agents use RichView
items.question: Does RichView measure how well agents use it, with fresh-agent runs on real tasks, scored and tracked over time, and does what the runs show drive changes to the agent surfaces?
items.why: Daniel's INT-21 answer makes agent-native authoring a headline bet at 100% and says measuring how well agents use RichView is a feature: fresh-agent runs on real tasks, scored and tracked over time, show where agents stumble, and RichView is changed so agents understand it as easily as possible. INT-69 sets the bar a fresh agent must clear and DEL-78 runs a pass-or-fail harness at each candidate, but no card defines the score, the real tasks or the history, so nobody could say whether the agent surfaces got better or worse after a change to `richview learn`, the skill, the MCP descriptions or a diagnostic.
items.proposed:
RichView measures how well agents use it, and the measurement is a feature, not only a gate (INT-21). A harness runs fresh agents on real tasks and scores each run.

- **Fresh agent:** a new session of a coding agent product, Claude Code and Codex first as DEL-78 sets, in an empty sandbox outside every checkout, with only the installed `richview` CLI and MCP server, no RichView source and a network limited to the model API.
- **Real task:** a brief a working analyst would give, with a dataset, a question and an audience, drawn from a rotating set built on real reports: the flagship's evidence, the example folders and public statistics. A toy prompt written to be easy is not a task.
- **Score:** per run, whether `richview check` ended clean and on which attempt; attempts and tool calls used; the tool errors and diagnostics the agent met; which of them it misread or could not act on; and whether the report meets the brief's checkable facts: the figures match the dataset, each requested chart type and table is present, and every chart names its source. The transcript, tool calls and final report are kept with the score.
- **History:** scores are stored per agent product, per RichView build and per task, and tracked over time, so a change to `richview learn`, the skill, an MCP description, a diagnostic or a default shows up as a change in the score.
- **What it drives:** each place agents stumble becomes a change to those surfaces, so agents understand RichView as easily as possible. The measurement never changes to fit a result.

The score measures RichView's agent surfaces. It judges nothing about whether the story argues well (INT-77), and a short or long source is neither rewarded nor penalized (INT-13). Runs use only RichView's own sandboxes and collect nothing from anyone's real use (INT-80, INT-82). INT-69 is the bar a run must clear and DEL-78 sets when the harness runs at the gate; this card defines the scoring, the task set and the history. The harness is development tooling in this repository, not a `richview` command. The score history is internal and shows in the review packet; a public claim about agent success needs a demonstration on richview.ai (INT-23, INT-65).

options.label: Scored fresh-agent runs, tracked over time
options.detail: Shows where agents stumble and whether a change helped; costs agent subscription usage per run, and the real tasks and the scoring need writing and keeping current.

options.label: Pass or fail at the gate only (DEL-78)
options.detail: Cheapest; says whether a candidate clears INT-69's bar, but not why, or how it trends, so the agent bet (INT-21) gets no feedback between candidates.

options.label: Scored runs and a public score
options.detail: The strongest evidence for the agent-native claim; a public number must be reproducible and pass INT-23's proof rule, and it adds a published artifact that needs Daniel's go.

items.recommendation: Scored fresh-agent runs, tracked over time: Daniel's INT-21 answer makes measuring agent use a feature, and a pass or fail at the gate cannot show where agents stumble.
